idiom_name: protocol-conforming wrapper type delegating to the wrapped instance (Vapor middleware for HTTP)
implementation_notes: Swift has no reflection-based proxying for protocol calls, so the interceptor is a hand-written wrapper that conforms to the same protocol and forwards: the audit logic is written once per audited method, then the call is passed to the inner instance, and callers see only the protocol so the wrapper is indistinguishable from the real service. In server applications Vapor's Middleware/AsyncMiddleware protocol is the idiomatic seam around a route handler, and it needs no wrapper type at all. The classic structure is still warranted when several concerns must compose (audit plus retry plus authorization) - small conforming structs composed at construction are the Swift-idiomatic form.
pitfalls: `any Payments` erases the concrete type, so composition must happen where the protocol is expected; code that holds the concrete type bypasses the wrapper entirely.
Async and throwing requirements must be forwarded exactly: changing the isolation (actor) or rethrowing differently breaks the protocol contract the caller depends on.
Value semantics: a struct wrapper is copied at each call site while the sink is usually a reference or actor - make sure the sink is the single shared instance, or records split across copies.
